title: Lorwyn Eclipsed Promos: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: "If even the simplest land-dweller can divert the river with no more than a shovel, just imagine what I can do."
Kithkin respect giants, but not usually from such close range.
Kithkin are bound through the thoughtweft—mind to mind and heart to heart.
"The home of the fae must be protected."
"This is *my* domain, and *I* am its Queen." —Maralen, fae ascendant
A song can unite quicker than a sword can divide.
If you stare long enough at your reflection, your reflection starts staring back.
Petals burst in evening hours with flitting things so fickle and sour.
"I will not rest until I have excised the rot from this land."
Maralen is more forgiving than Oona was, but her rule is no less absolute.
"Finally, a place where the ingredients are as potent as my magics!"
Flamekin believe it knows the slopes of Mount Kulrath even better than they do.
"Charge! Aim for the cuticles!"
The only metal polish he uses is blood.
Heart calmed by the beauty of the blossom, the dawnhand wondered who was actually protecting whom.
Jean-Emmanuel Depraz, World Champion XXIX
No matter their size, strength, or demeanor, the brave stand side by side.
The right poem lifts more than spirits.
"Each year that passes rots you with scars. Shelter your heart, for the world is cruel."
Faeries swarm to snoring boggarts like vultures to rotting meat.
Kirol hated being a pawn in Morcant's game. If dawnglove was as potent as she suggested, it should be preserved, not used to tip the balance of power.
"I know I belong somewhere—just not here."
"Keep enemies close . . . and elves closer." —A tale of Auntie Wort
"What are the odds? And what would you like them to be?"
"For those we lost, that they may forever live." —Tapestry inscription
Forged in Velis Vel, swiped by a clever merrow, and sold to a curious kithkin.
The boggart was playfully prodding a critter when the skies darkened, then he gobbled it down with glee.
The merrow was vending her wares when the skies darkened, then she sharply raised her prices.
The elf was disgusted by the bramble before him when the skies darkened, then he stepped closer to observe the wild beauty.
The flamekin was drawn toward warm laughter when the skies darkened, then she turned back to the lonely peak.
The kithkin was admiring the flowers when the skies darkened, then they ripped up the roots for the next season.
